## Review status

I am still actively reviewing Paul Banyard's performance, pipeline discipline, and agreed actions from our weekly and monthly check-ins. These notes are my working record — typed in first person for handover continuity — and reflect what we discussed, what we agreed, and what remains under scrutiny. Nothing here is a final sign-off. The pattern across March to July is one of strong individual months punctuated by workflow slippage, protection attachment collapse, and income drift against a rising bank threshold. I am watching whether the July process changes (Platform consolidation, Tue/Thu/Fri team updates, Edinburgh lead mining) stick, or whether we see the same backlog rebuild we saw after annual leave in June.

## Trends I'm seeing (each under review)

### Task and workflow backlog — under review

This is the single most recurring critical risk on Paul's book. Overdue Platform and Midas tasks have peaked at **59** (2026-06-24, post–annual leave), then **27** with **8** late (2026-07-01), then roughly **15** overdue with some tasks **~35 days** old (2026-07-08). The failure mode is not always neglect — Paul often prioritises live cases or complex research — but the effect is identical: unworked leads, SLA breaches, and estimated revenue leakage of **£3–4k** from backlog alone (Paul's own estimate at 24 June). What I am specifically watching is cosmetic date-rolling: moving tasks forward in the diary without a genuine call, email, bin, or stage change. The 1 July review showed improvement — queue cut **27 → 8** (**70%** reduction), dead leads binned, calls before emails — but by 8 July we were back to **~15** overdue. Dual working across Midas and Platform remains a structural problem; we agreed Platform as single source of truth for spoken-to prospects, with dummy-client workflow practice, but I have not yet seen that fully embedded.

### Lead contact, conversion, and Edinburgh pipeline — under review

Year-to-date to June, **67** leads with **47%** never contacted is unacceptable and directly tied to the income shortfall narrative. February/March lead views showed large "unable to contact" pools (**66%** unable to contact/no-show on a **359**-lead view in early March; February **34** leads with only **1** DIP). Edinburgh lead flow stalled mid-year, then we pivoted to rebuilding via "mortgage arranged elsewhere" mining, daily lead emails, saved report filters ("Paul's Active View"), and strict use of the **Edinburgh Markets** booking link (plus New Homes where relevant). Wrong booking links used by teams break attribution — flagged again on **2026-07-08** with **82** leads YTD and **18** from Edinburgh. Core Edinburgh purchase market framed as **£250k+**, household income **£70k–£200k+**. Peak diary slots for bookings cited as **09:30, 11:00, 14:30, 15:30** — Paul should not block large chunks that prevent those slots filling. Referrer re-engagement (Priya, Kate, Max, John, Alex, Brody) and Dalton Y / Dalton Wybar cadence are part of this same thread.

### Tue / Thu / Fri update emails (CC Bob) — under review

Agreed from **2026-06-24** onward: **5–10 minute** team catch-ups on **Tuesday, Thursday, Friday** mornings, each followed by a Financial Services update email **CC'ing me (Bob)**. Consistency is the core failure mode — Paul himself acknowledged that when this slips, it slips very quickly. The 8 July session reinforced lead-outcome update emails on the same cadence, catch-ups with Max, John, Alex, Brody on patches/market, and my reminding teams of the Edinburgh Markets link. I am monitoring whether these emails actually land three times a week and whether they contain lead outcomes, not generic commentary.

## Why we keep monitoring

Paul is capable of record months and is respected in the team — both of which matter for collaboration and recovery. March **2026** proved he can write **£28,839.33** and submit **12** mortgage apps in a month. The concern is not baseline skill; it is sustainability of process under volume and after absence. When workflow control slips, lead contact rates collapse (**47%** uncontacted YTD), protection attachment collapses (**25%** purchases), and income gaps compound toward ~**£20k** against a rising **£21,750** monthly bank threshold. Clients in Edinburgh and Scotland markets are finding properties in **15–25 days** on average — slow follow-up loses them to competitors, including viewers who already have a DIP before a viewing. Edinburgh attribution depends on correct **Edinburgh Markets** links; wrong links corrupt the very reports we built to recover lead flow. Protection revenue and client outcomes are both at stake — underinsured purchase clients and missed post-offer windows were recurring themes from March onward. Finally, compliance exposure on FTB/BTL intent, mortgage-into-retirement documentation, and file-note quality creates regulatory risk beyond pure revenue. I keep monitoring because the July improvements (task reduction, two policies written, compliance escalation on Gary) are real but fragile — we have seen backlogs rebuild from **12** overdues in March to **59** in June before.
